title: GOD PROVIDES FOR THOSE WHO SERVE HIM

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the Lord said to Aaron, "I myself have put you in charge of the offerings presented to me; all the holy offerings the Israelites give me I give to you and your sons as your portion, your perpetual share. You are to have the part of the most holy offerings that is kept from the fire. From all the gifts they bring me as most holy offerings, whether grain or sin or guilt offerings, that part belongs to you and your sons." — Num 18:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The priests owned no farmland and had no crops of their own, because their whole life was devoted to serving God. So how would they live? God Himself answers: "I myself have put you in charge of the offerings." The Lord became their provision. What the people brought to God, God gave to those who served Him.

This is a beautiful principle. When God calls people to give themselves fully to His work, He takes responsibility for their needs. The priests did not have to worry about how they would eat, because God had arranged their provision through the offerings of His people. Those who served at the altar were fed from the altar.

We can trust the same God today. He is no one's debtor. When we give ourselves to serve Him, we are not left to fend for ourselves. This is not a promise of wealth or ease — the priests received a portion, not riches — but a promise that God faithfully provides what His servants need. He cares for those who care for His work.

Ultimately, all these offerings pointed to Christ, the one perfect offering. The priests fed on the sacrifices; we feed on Him. Jesus said He is the bread of life, and those who come to Him will never go hungry. Whatever your calling, you can serve God without anxious fear about your needs, because the God who provided for the priests provides for you, and has given you His Son as your true and lasting portion.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you trust God to provide as you give yourself to His work?
2. How have you seen God faithfully meet your needs in the past?
3. What does it mean that Christ Himself is your true portion?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You faithfully provide for those who serve You. Free me from anxious worry about my needs, and help me to trust Your care. Thank You that Christ is the bread of life and my lasting portion. Amen.
